hypothesis: If eggs are never oblate, then in a large cross-species sample of measured bird eggs essentially none has length (polar axis) shorter than maximum breadth (equatorial axis), i.e. elongation L/B is at least 1 for all species.
pass_criterion: Species-mean L/B (egg length divided by maximum breadth) is at least 0.98 for 100% of species, AND at least 99% of individual eggs have L/B >= 0.98, AND no species has an L/B 95% confidence interval lying wholly below 0.98 (the 0.98 margin allows for measurement error).
fail_criterion: Any species with mean L/B < 0.95 and n >= 5 eggs, OR more than 1% of individual eggs with L/B < 0.95, OR two or more species whose L/B 95% CI lies wholly below 0.98, after removing records flagged as data-entry errors (e.g. L/B < 0.7 or > 2.5).
interpretation: Thompson's 'prolate spheroid' means a solid of revolution whose polar axis (egg length) exceeds its equatorial diameter (maximum breadth); 'oblate/flattened/discoidal' means the polar axis is shorter than the equatorial. Mapped to measurable quantities: L/B from egg length and maximum breadth of hard-shelled bird eggs, with L/B > 1 prolate and L/B < 1 oblate. Modern reinterpretation: real eggs are asymmetric (ovoid), not exact spheroids, so the test checks only the axis-ratio criterion (prolate vs oblate), not exact spheroid geometry. Near-spherical eggs (L/B about 1, e.g. some owls, kingfishers) are not counted as oblate unless clearly below the tolerance. The test covers hard-shelled bird eggs, which is the dataset's scope.

dataset.name: Data from: The evolution of egg shape in birds: Evolutionary constraints and adaptations
dataset.why_it_fits: Public Dryad dataset with downloadable CSVs: DATAraweggs.csv (individual egg measurements) and DATAeggshape.csv (species-level egg shape/elongation). Fields to use: species identifier, egg length and egg breadth (or the elongation index) to compute L/B per egg and per species. Exact column names must be confirmed from README.txt before analysis; they could not be confirmed from the landing page.
